title: Automatic Generation of Mappings for Distributed Fourier Operations
problem: Distributed Fourier transform libraries provide rigid implementations forcing developers to mold code around FFT computations, missing opportunities to minimize communication between Fourier operations and surrounding numerical computations.
motivation: Fourier transforms are ubiquitous in scientific computing but are often communication-bottlenecked in distributed settings. Flexible mapping of Fourier operations to processes can significantly reduce inter-kernel communication.
method: Automatic mapping generation for multi-dimensional distributed Fourier operations using novel non-linear iterative formulation. Leverages Z3 SMT solver to optimize across both Fourier and linear algebra operations, minimizing communication steps across key MPI collectives while selecting optimal grid shape.
key_novelty: Automated optimization framework combining SMT solving with Fourier and linear algebra scheduling to minimize communication across distributed computations.
contributions: Automatic mapping generation for distributed Fourier operations
SMT-based optimization across Fourier and linear algebra kernels
Joint optimization of grid shape and communication patterns
2-31x speedup compared to coupled heFFTe+COSMA solutions
Enables developer-specified computation flows rather than framework constraints
limitations: Specific benchmarks and workload characteristics not detailed in abstract.
